title: Fractions Through Sewing
topic: Fractions: halves, quarters, eighths and joining them
description: Lens course only this app would make. Every fraction is a piece of fabric. Cut, measure, and join: halves, quarters, and eighths on the cutting mat, with seam allowance you can measure.
author: Well of Wisdom contributors

lessons.title: Halves and quarters on the mat
lessons.summary: A yard is the whole. Cut it into equal pieces and name what you have.

content.title: A yard is the whole
content.body:
On a cutting mat a yard of fabric is the whole, that is $1$. Cut it with one straight cut down the middle and each piece is one half, written $\frac{1}{2}$. Cut each half again and you have quarters, $\frac{1}{4}$. Quarters are smaller than halves because the same yard is cut into more pieces.

- $1$ yard cut into $2$ is halves: $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{2}$
- $1$ yard cut into $4$ is quarters: $\frac{1}{4}$ four times
- $\frac{2}{4}$ is the same length as $\frac{1}{2}$

content.prompt: Which piece is longer, one half yard or one quarter yard?
content.explanation: A half is one of two pieces, a quarter is one of four. Two pieces make bigger pieces than four, so one half yard is longer.
content.hint: Cut the same yard two ways. Which makes bigger pieces?

content.prompt: How many quarter-yard pieces make a whole yard?
content.hint: Stack quarters until you reach a yard.

lessons.title: Seam allowance
lessons.summary: Measure what the seam takes and what is left to show.

content.title: What the seam allowance eats
content.body:
A pattern says: cut $\frac{3}{8}$ yard, seam allowance $\frac{1}{8}$ yard, finished piece $\frac{1}{4}$ yard. That checks out because $\frac{3}{8} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{2}{8}$ and $\frac{2}{8} = \frac{1}{4}$. The seam takes one eighth, a quarter stays visible.

- Finished length = cut length minus seam allowance
- $\frac{2}{8}$ renamed as eighths is still $\frac{2}{8}$, which is $\frac{1}{4}$

content.prompt: You cut $\frac{5}{8}$ yard and the seam allowance is $\frac{1}{8}$ yard. How much is left to show, as eighths? Give the numerator.
Explain why $\frac{2}{4}$ of a yard and $\frac{4}{8}$ of a yard are the same length, using the mat.
content.answer: Cut a yard into 4 and take 2 pieces, or cut a yard into 8 and take 4. Both cover half a yard, because 2 out of 4 and 4 out of 8 are each one half.
content.explanation: Any answer that names both as one half is right.

content.title: Measure the mat
content.description: Take a paper strip for a yard. Mark halves, then quarters, then eighths, each in a different colour. Lay a ruler beside it and cut paper pieces $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{4}$, $\frac{3}{8}$ and $\frac{5}{8}$ yard. Tape them to a page and label each with its fraction and one sentence about what you kept seeing.
content.rubric:
- Halves, quarters and eighths are evenly spaced and coloured
- Four pieces cut to length and labelled
- One sentence compares two pieces correctly
